question: If x + y = 10 and xy = 24.96 , then find the value of (x − y)² .
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use identity: (x − y)² = (x + y)² − 4xy

= 10² − 4 × 24.96

= 100 − 99.84

= 0.16

**∴ Answer = 0.16**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x + y = 10, xy = 24.96

**Formula used:**

(x − y)² = (x + y)² − 4xy

**Calculation:**

⇒ (x − y)² = (10)² − 4 × 24.96

⇒ = 100 − 99.84

⇒ = 0.16

**∴ The correct answer is 0.16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity

(x − y)² = x² + y² − 2xy

Useful Identity

(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

Derived Relation

(x − y)² = (x + y)² − 4xy

Application Tip

When sum and product are given, use identities instead of solving variables.
